tagline: The Riviera's gateway airport sits metres from the sea, yet every onward hop to Monaco, Cannes and Cap Ferrat still goes by congested coast road — the water is the open lane.
summary: Nice is the front door to the French Riviera: its waterfront airport handled 14.8 million passengers in 2024 and a record 15.2 million in 2025, making it France's busiest airport outside Paris and the arrival point for millions of leisure and high-net-worth travellers heading to Monaco, Cannes, Cap Ferrat and beyond. Today those onward legs mean a slow crawl along the Basse Corniche and the A8, or a €195 helicopter seat to Monaco for those who can pay to skip the jam. The Baie des Anges is calm, the distances are short, and the gateway already touches the water — making Nice the natural anchor for a clean, fast foiling network that turns the coast road's worst bottlenecks into smooth, near-silent sea hops.

use_cases.title: Airport-to-coast premium transfers
use_cases.body: Step off a flight and onto a foiling craft on the Baie des Anges, arriving in Monaco, Cap Ferrat or Cannes without ever touching the gridlocked Corniche. A smooth, near-silent sea transfer that competes head-on with the helicopter on comfort and arrival experience.

use_cases.title: Riviera coastal express line
use_cases.body: A high-frequency foiling shuttle linking Nice with Antibes, Cannes and Monaco along the busiest stretch of the Côte d'Azur. It bypasses the A8 and the coast road entirely, turning a stop-start drive into a fast, reliable crossing on flat coastal water.

use_cases.title: Day-trip and excursion gateway
use_cases.body: On-demand foiling runs from central Nice to the marquee day-trip destinations of the Riviera and, with the hybrid platform, across open water to Corsica. Visitors trade the queue and the carbon for a signature on-water arrival.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The core Riviera legs anchored on Nice all sit comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on calm coastal water — Nice→Monaco (~8 nm), Nice→Antibes (~9 nm) and Nice→Cannes (~16 nm) — leaving ample margin for high-frequency daily rotations from the airport and city harbour.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The 2,000 nm hybrid range extends the network down-coast to Saint-Tropez (~50 nm) and across open water to Corsica (~95 nm) or the Italian Riviera, where grid charging isn't viable, turning Nice into the mainland hub for longer experiential and inter-regional corridors.
